stories.title: EU consults on sustainability reporting standards
stories.summary: The EU has launched a consultation on assurance standards for sustainability reporting. Large companies must report their sustainability performance under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, with information requiring independent review to be considered credible. The consultation is open to auditors, investors, and companies preparing reports.

stories.title: DitchCarbon adds electricity module to supply chain platform
stories.summary: DitchCarbon has launched an electricity module for its Scope 3 emissions platform. The feature aims to help procurement teams identify tier 1 suppliers that could reduce emissions by switching to low-carbon electricity. The company describes this as one of the fastest levers for supply chain decarbonization.

stories.title: CEO misconduct exits rise
stories.summary: CEO departures attributed to misconduct have doubled compared to 2024. Andy Challenger, chief revenue officer for Challenger, Gray & Christmas, stated that these exits are no longer just a matter of romance or morality, but a question of judgment.

stories.title: Anthropic receives high ESG risk rating before IPO
stories.summary: Sustainalytics has designated Anthropic as a high ESG risk ahead of its upcoming IPO. The rating is driven by concerns regarding business ethics and human capital management at the AI company.

stories.title: Juventus publishes 13th sustainability report
stories.summary: Juventus has released its 13th sustainability report, marking its second year using the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive framework. The club is the first and only Italian football team to adopt these requirements, which are integrated into its annual financial report and subject to independent assurance.

stories.title: FRC seeks more accountability in stewardship reports
stories.summary: The Financial Reporting Council has called for greater detail on manager accountability in its first review of reporting under the revised UK code. Signatories are expected to provide more information regarding how they scrutinize the performance and actions of their external managers.

stories.title: Fujitsu targets net-zero at business sites by 2030
stories.summary: Fujitsu plans to reach net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions at its sites by fiscal 2030. The company will use nature-based carbon removal credits and renewable energy through virtual power purchase agreements. It has already signed a 15-year credit procurement deal with Tokyo Gas.

stories.title: Nextpower reports 12 percent reduction in Scope 3 emissions
stories.summary: Nextpower has published its third sustainability report, noting a 12 percent reduction in Scope 3 emissions intensity. The company highlighted its SBTi validation and expanded use of third-party assurance and lower-carbon steel across its global supply chain and technology solutions platform.

stories.title: Carbon market report highlights supply-demand gap
stories.summary: A report released at COP31 identifies $70.9 billion in potential carbon credit supply through 2030, while only $1.6 billion has been contracted by sovereign buyers. The data suggests a significant imbalance between the volume of credits being prepared and actual demand from governments.

stories.title: S’pore seals carbon credit deal with Kenya, its third African partner | The Straits Times - newspaper - Magzter
Norway to purchase carbon credits from Indonesia and Morocco
stories.summary: The Norwegian government has agreed to purchase up to 12 million tons of carbon credits from Indonesia and 8.78 million tons from Morocco over 10 years. Climate Minister Sigrun Aasland stated the agreements demonstrate the role of international cooperation in accelerating the energy transition.

stories.title: Norway Signs 10-Year Carbon Credit Deals With Morocco and Indonesia - Barlaman Today
EU allows partial deduction of CBAM fees
stories.summary: EU-based companies importing commodities under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism may now deduct carbon credits from their fees. These deductions are capped at 10 percent of the total obligation.

stories.title: Singapore expands carbon market partnerships
stories.summary: Singapore has authorized its first carbon credit project in Rwanda and signed a trading agreement with Bangladesh at COP31. The Rwanda project aims to reduce 780,000 tonnes of CO2 by distributing water filters. The deals are intended to turn partnerships into practical climate finance projects.

stories.title: Norway finalizes 10-year carbon credit deals
stories.summary: Norway has confirmed agreements to buy carbon credits from Morocco and Indonesia over a decade. The government stated the revenue will support renewable energy development in both countries. The deals were concluded under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement to facilitate international emission cuts.

stories.title: Korea joins international carbon market coalition
stories.summary: Korea has joined the Carbon Market Club of Clubs, an international coalition that includes the EU and China. The country will participate in setting global rules for carbon trading and offset credits. The announcement was made during the COP31 climate conference in Türkiye.

stories.title: GCC and Turkish energy exchange sign cooperation deal
stories.summary: The Global Carbon Council and Türkiye’s Energy Exchange have signed a memorandum of understanding to cooperate on carbon market development. The agreement, signed at COP31, aims to explore opportunities for trading GCC-issued carbon credits within the Turkish market.

stories.title: COP31 Carbon Market Reality Check: $71 Billion Credit Pipeline but Only $1.6 Billion Contracted as Buyers Question Emiss
stories.summary: COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye, have exposed a major imbalance in international carbon markets: governments and project developers are preparing billions of tonnes of carbon credits for sale, but actual transactions, verified emission reductions and financing reaching climate projects remain far smaller. A new COP31 report identifies $70.9 billion

stories.title: Climate negotiations enter final days in Antalya
stories.summary: The first draft of the COP31 agreement contains 144 separate items, many of which remain under dispute. Negotiators are currently debating language on fossil fuel transitions and financial support for developing nations. The summit is scheduled to conclude in four days, with much still on the table.

stories.title: COP31 draft text offers two options on fossil fuel phase-out - Utilities Middle East
Finance gaps persist at COP31
stories.summary: Nearly 200 governments are meeting in Antalya to address the discrepancy between climate promises and available funding. While new initiatives aim to assist with project preparation, they do not replace the public finance required by emerging economies. Disagreements remain as the summit enters its final week.

stories.title: COP31 deal draft foreshadows difficult route to consensus - France 24
COP31 draft proposes fossil fuel phaseout
stories.summary: Australia has released a draft political deal calling for an accelerated phaseout of coal, oil, and gas. The document requires approval from nearly 200 nations by Friday. The talks are currently navigating a difficult backdrop of geopolitical tensions and an ongoing energy crisis.

stories.title: Electrification pledge faces resistance at COP31
stories.summary: Major developing countries have signaled they will not support a firm commitment to boost global electrification to 35 percent by 2035. The summit is currently focusing on this target as an alternative to reducing fossil fuel production. Electricity currently accounts for 23 percent of global consumption.

stories.title: Ministers clash over COP31 cover text
stories.summary: The second week of the UN climate conference has opened with pushback from fossil-fuel producers and large developing nations. These groups have stated they do not want new sectoral targets included in the final cover decision, specifically opposing the electrification pledge proposed by the Turkish presidency.

stories.title: Political shifts offer breathing space for climate talks
stories.summary: The Guardian suggests that recent election results in Brazil and the United States have provided political relief for the COP31 process. The editorial notes that the re-election of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Democratic gains in the US midterms may influence future climate policy trajectories.

stories.title: Ecomondo platform evolves for green transition
stories.summary: Ecomondo has transitioned from a waste and recycling fair into a platform for the green transition. Exhibition manager Mauro Delle Fratte states the event has repeatedly reinvented itself by responding to and anticipating market changes. The platform now emphasizes biogas, biomethane, and regenerative agriculture.

stories.title: Mexico explores Chinese waste-to-energy models
stories.summary: Environment Minister Alicia Bárcena visited Chinese facilities to study waste utilization and water restoration technologies. Mexico aims to transition its waste management strategy toward an energy-from-waste model to solve disposal problems and reclaim public spaces currently used for landfills.

stories.title: IEA provides waste-to-energy advice to COP31
stories.summary: The Turkish presidency of the UN climate conference has requested advice from the International Energy Agency regarding the synergy between waste reduction and sustainable energy systems. The IEA is currently consulting on how waste management can contribute to broader emissions reduction goals.

stories.title: Report estimates zero waste emissions potential
stories.summary: Research released at COP31 suggests that waste prevention and material efficiency could avoid 149 billion tonnes of greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The estimate is conditional on the implementation of specific measures. The authors note these are potential avoided emissions rather than reductions already achieved.

stories.title: Italy reports non-compliance in green procurement
stories.summary: Monitoring of public contracts in Italy shows a 36.5 percent non-compliance rate for road infrastructure and 23.2 percent for construction regarding Minimum Environmental Criteria. These standards are mandatory for public procurement, yet failure to meet them is reportedly hindering the circular economy.

stories.title: 2026 CCAC Challenge Programme to Unlocking Value from Organic Waste: Building Markets for Circular Economy Solutions - C
Ghana urged to adopt circular waste management
stories.summary: The University of Environment and Sustainable Development and the Environmental Protection Authority have called for stronger enforcement of environmental laws in Ghana. They advocate for a shift toward recycling and resource recovery to address growing waste management challenges and promote job creation.

stories.title: Libya presents circular economy strategy at COP31
stories.summary: Libya presented a waste management strategy during the COP31 conference in Antalya. The lecture, hosted by the International Solid Waste Association, examined current solid waste management challenges in the country and explored practical solutions for developing a waste-free future.

stories.title: Resource efficiency conference concludes in Colombo
stories.summary: The 4th International Conference on Resource Efficiency and Circular Economy has concluded in Colombo. The event focused on the role of sustainable industrial growth within Sri Lanka.

stories.title: Amazon commits $7 billion to Indian renewable energy
stories.summary: Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, adding to $4 billion already contracted. The company announced four new wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts, including its largest wind project in Asia to date.

stories.title: Pace Digitek secures 2,691 crore BESS order from NTPC Green Energy
stories.summary: Pace Digitek has secured a 2,691 crore order from NTPC Green Energy for a 600 MW battery energy storage system at the Khavda Solar Plant. The contract covers engineering, procurement, construction, and 15 years of maintenance. The company describes this as its largest battery storage contract to date.

stories.title: BPCL plans green jet fuel plant at Mumbai refinery
stories.summary: BPCL is developing a sustainable aviation fuel facility at its Mumbai refinery as part of a 1,400 crore green aviation strategy. The refiner has created indigenous catalyst technology to convert used cooking oil into bio-jet fuel. The project aims to support net-zero operational emissions by 2040.

stories.title: Luminous Power eyes 3x revenue by 2030
stories.summary: Luminous Power Technologies plans to triple its revenue by 2030 compared to 2025 levels. The company intends to scale its residential rooftop solar business by moving from individual components to complete systems including panels, inverters, and installation services. The target covers the company's overall business growth.

stories.title: SECI targets 10 GW own capacity by 2030
stories.summary: The Solar Energy Corporation of India is targeting 10 GW of owned renewable capacity by 2030. The state-run entity is also pursuing maharatna status while expanding into battery storage and green ammonia. The shift follows a national focus on reliable power supply and domestic manufacturing for clean energy.

stories.title: Energy storage firms raise 16.7 billion in corporate funding
stories.summary: Energy storage companies raised 16.7 billion in corporate funding during the first nine months of 2026. Venture capital funding rose 93 percent to 5.4 billion across 79 deals. The total number of transactions reached a five-year high, while project acquisitions more than doubled to 21.6 GW.

stories.title: GM backs 550 million solar investment
stories.summary: General Motors has signed a deal for 276 MW of energy, serving as the primary customer for two new solar facilities in Michigan. GM says the 550 million project will generate 539,000 megawatt-hours of electricity annually. The automaker previously claimed to have matched its U.S. electricity consumption with renewables.

stories.title: Schneider Electric Infrastructure positions for capex wave
stories.summary: Schneider Electric Infrastructure reported a 19.8 percent year-on-year sales increase to 779 crore for the second quarter of 2027. The company is currently trading at a price-to-earnings ratio of 148, significantly higher than the industry average of 32.3. The stock remains 31 percent below its 52-week high.
